title: "Check model approach"
format: html

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(here)
source(here("utils","check_packages.R"))
source(here("utils","functions.R"))
load(here("data", "data_constructed", "mar_table.RData"))
```


Lets create a function that will calculate the log-odds ratio and its standard error from `tab-mar` for two groups.

```{r}
calculate_or <- function(group1, group2) {
  lor <- log(tab_mar[group1, group2,])+log(tab_mar[group2, group1,])-
    log(tab_mar[group1, group1,])-log(tab_mar[group2, group2,])
  se <- sqrt(1/tab_mar[group1, group2,]+1/tab_mar[group2, group1,]+
               1/tab_mar[group1, group1,]+1/tab_mar[group2, group2,])
  tibble(year = as.numeric(names(lor)), lor, se, 
         type = paste(group1, group2, sep="-"))
}
```

We can now use `pmap` to calculate log odds ratios across all groups of interest.

```{r}
#| label: get-lor-df

all_combos <- tribble(
  ~race1, ~race2,
  "White", "Black",
  "White", "AIAN",
  "White", "API",
  "White", "Hispanic",
  "Black", "AIAN",
  "Black", "API",
  "Black", "Hispanic",
  "AIAN", "API",
  "AIAN", "Hispanic",
  "API", "Hispanic",
  "White/Black", "White",
  "White/Black", "Black",
  "White/API", "White",
  "White/API", "API",
  "White/AIAN", "White",
  "White/AIAN", "AIAN"
)

lor_data <- pmap(all_combos, function(race1, race2) {
  calculate_or(race1, race2)
  }) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  filter(lor > -Inf)
```

Now lets try a model approach.

First convert to a frequency based dataset

```{r}
mar_data_full <- as.data.frame.table(tab_mar) |>
  tibble() |>
  rename(race_husband = Var1, race_wife = Var2, year = Var3, freq = Freq) |>
  filter(year != 1960)
```


## Two-group case

Start with two groups. By default you will get an endogamy parameter so switch this to an intermarriage parameter.

```{r}
mar_data_white_black <- mar_data_full |>
  filter(race_husband %in% c("White", "Black") & 
           race_wife %in% c("White", "Black")) |>
  mutate(inter_w_b = (race_husband == "White" & race_wife == "Black"))

model_wb <- glm(freq~(race_husband + race_wife + inter_w_b) * year, 
                data = mar_data_white_black, family = poisson)

wb_lor <- avg_slopes(model_wb, variables = "inter_w_b", by = "year", 
                     type = "link")
```

How does this compare to cross-product?

```{r}

temp <- wb_lor |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(paste(year))) |>
  rename(lor_model = estimate, se_model = std.error) |>
  select(lor_model, se_model, year)

temp <- lor_data |> 
  filter(type == "White-Black") |>
  rename(lor_cross = lor, se_cross = se) |>
  select(-type) |>
  inner_join(temp)
  
ggplot(temp, aes(x = lor_cross, y = lor_model))+
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "red")+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x = "White/Black log odds ratio by cross-product",
       y = "White/Black lod odds ratio by model")+
  #geom_text_repel(aes(label = year))+
  theme_bw()

ggplot(temp, aes(x = se_cross, y = se_model))+
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "red")+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x = "White/Black log odds ratio standard error by cross-product",
       y = "White/Black lod odds ratio standard error by model")+
  theme_bw()
```

Perfect fit.

## Three-group case

Now we have a spare parameter to fit.

```{r}
mar_data_three_group <- mar_data_full |>
  filter(race_husband %in% c("White", "Black", "API") & 
           race_wife %in% c("White", "Black", "API")) |>
  mutate(inter_w_b = (race_husband == "White" & race_wife == "Black"),
         inter_w_a = (race_husband == "White" & race_wife == "API"),
         inter_b_a = (race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "API"),
         gender_b_a = case_when(
           race_husband == "API" & race_wife == "Black" ~ 1,
           race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "API" ~ -1,
           TRUE ~ 0
         ))

model_three_group <- glm(freq~(race_husband + race_wife + 
                                 inter_w_b +
                                 inter_w_a + 
                                 inter_b_a + 
                                 gender_b_a) * year, 
                data = mar_data_three_group, family = poisson)

inter_lor <- avg_slopes(model_three_group, 
                        variables = c("inter_w_b", "inter_w_a", "inter_b_a"), 
                        by = "year", 
                        type = "link")
```



```{r}

temp <- inter_lor |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(paste(year)),
    type = case_when(
      term == "inter_w_b" ~ "White-Black",
      term == "inter_w_a" ~ "White-API",
      term == "inter_b_a" ~ "Black-API",
    )
  ) |>
  rename(lor_model = estimate, se_model = std.error) |>
  select(lor_model, se_model, year, type)

temp <- lor_data |> 
  filter(type %in% c("White-Black", "White-API", "Black-API")) |>
  rename(lor_cross = lor, se_cross = se) |>
  inner_join(temp)
  
ggplot(temp, aes(x = lor_cross, y = lor_model))+
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "red")+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x = "White/Black log odds ratio by cross-product",
       y = "White/Black lod odds ratio by model")+
  facet_wrap(~type)+
  theme_bw()

ggplot(temp, aes(x = se_cross, y = se_model))+
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "red")+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x = "White/Black log odds ratio standard error by cross-product",
       y = "White/Black lod odds ratio standard error by model")+
  facet_wrap(~type)+
  theme_bw()
```


# All single race groups

Sparseness problems are created for years where we get zero cells. This causes all of the SEs in the AMEs to be wrong. Filtering out frequencies of zero seems to fix the problem. The `avg_slopes` gives a warning about rank deficient matrices but it fits everything fine.

```{r}
mar_data_single <- mar_data_full |>
  #filter(year != "1970") |>
  filter(!str_detect(race_husband, "/|Other"), 
         !str_detect(race_wife, "/|Other")) |>
  filter(freq > 0) |>
  mutate(
    inter_w_b = (race_husband == "White" & race_wife == "Black"),
    inter_w_a = (race_husband == "White" & race_wife == "API"),
    inter_w_i = (race_husband == "White" & race_wife == "AIAN"),
    inter_w_h = (race_husband == "White" & race_wife == "Hispanic"),
    inter_b_a = (race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "API"),
    inter_b_i = (race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "AIAN"),
    inter_b_h = (race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "Hispanic"),
    inter_a_i = (race_husband == "API" & race_wife == "AIAN"),
    inter_a_h = (race_husband == "API" & race_wife == "Hispanic"),
    inter_i_h = (race_husband == "AIAN" & race_wife == "Hispanic"),
    gender_b_a = case_when(
      race_husband == "API" & race_wife == "Black" ~ 1,
      race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "API" ~ -1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    gender_b_i = case_when(
      race_husband == "AIAN" & race_wife == "Black" ~ 1,
      race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "AIAN" ~ -1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    gender_b_h = case_when(
      race_husband == "Hispanic" & race_wife == "Black" ~ 1,
      race_husband == "Black" & race_wife == "Hispanic" ~ -1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    gender_a_i = case_when(
      race_husband == "AIAN" & race_wife == "API" ~ 1,
      race_husband == "API" & race_wife == "AIAN" ~ -1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    gender_a_h = case_when(
      race_husband == "Hispanic" & race_wife == "API" ~ 1,
      race_husband == "API" & race_wife == "Hispanic" ~ -1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    gender_i_h = case_when(
      race_husband == "Hispanic" & race_wife == "AIAN" ~ 1,
      race_husband == "AIAN" & race_wife == "Hispanic" ~ -1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )

model_single <- glm(freq~(race_husband + race_wife + 
                            inter_w_b +
                            inter_w_a + 
                            inter_w_i +
                            inter_w_h + 
                            inter_b_a + 
                            inter_b_i +
                            inter_b_h +
                            inter_a_i + 
                            inter_a_h + 
                            inter_i_h + 
                            gender_b_a +
                            gender_b_i + 
                            gender_b_h + 
                            gender_a_i +
                            gender_a_h + 
                            gender_i_h) * year, 
                data = mar_data_single, family = poisson)

inter_lor <- avg_slopes(model_single, 
                        variables = c("inter_w_b", 
                                      "inter_w_a",
                                      "inter_w_i",
                                      "inter_w_h",
                                      "inter_b_a",
                                      "inter_b_i",
                                      "inter_b_h",
                                      "inter_a_i",
                                      "inter_a_h",
                                      "inter_i_h"), 
                        by = "year", 
                        type = "link")
```


```{r}

temp <- inter_lor |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(paste(year)),

      term == "inter_w_a" ~ "White-API",

temp <- lor_data |>
```

# Try automating


```{r}
selected_groups <- c("White", "Black", "AIAN", "API", "Hispanic")

mar_data <- mar_data_full |>
  filter(race_husband %in% selected_groups & race_wife %in% selected_groups) |>
  filter(freq > 0)

for(i in 1:(length(selected_groups)-1)) {
  for(j in (i+1):length(selected_groups)) {
    
    race1 <- selected_groups[i]
    race2 <- selected_groups[j]
    
    var_suffix <- paste(str_to_lower(race1), str_to_lower(race2), sep = "_")
    var_suffix <- str_replace(var_suffix, "/", ".")
    
    var_name <- paste0("inter_", var_suffix)                 
    mar_data <- mar_data |>
      mutate({{ var_name }} := (race_husband == race1 & race_wife == race2))
    
    if(i > 1) {
      # we need a gender adjuster
      var_name <- paste0("gender_", var_suffix)
      mar_data <- mar_data |>
        mutate(
          {{ var_name }} := case_when(
            race_husband == race1 & race_wife == race2 ~ 1,
            race_husband ==  race2 & race_wife ==  race1 ~ -1,
            TRUE ~ 0
          )
        )
    }
  }
}

create_formula <- function(mar_data) {
  terms <- colnames(mar_data)
  terms <- terms[-which(terms == "year")]
  terms <- terms[-which(terms == "freq")]
  terms <- paste0("(", paste(terms, collapse="+"), ")*year")
  reformulate(terms, "freq")
}

model <- glm(create_formula(mar_data), data = mar_data, family = poisson)

terms <- colnames(mar_data)[str_detect(colnames(mar_data), "^inter_")]

inter_lor <- avg_slopes(model, variables = terms, by = "year", type = "link")

inter_lor |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(paste(year))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = exp(estimate), color = term))+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2000, linetype = 2)+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = exp(conf.low), ymax = exp(conf.high), fill = term),
              alpha = 0.3, color = NA)+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(size = 0.5)+
  scale_y_log10()+
  theme_bw()
```


# All groups

Is there a way where we can do this more programmatically for all the groups?

```{r}


# restrict marriage data to what is in all_combos
mar_data <- pmap(all_combos, function(race1, race2) {
  mar_data |>
    filter((race_husband == race1 & race_wife == race2) |
             (race_husband == race2 & race_wife == race1))
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

for(i in 1:nrow(all_combos)) {
    
    race1 <- all_combos$race1[i]
    race2 <- all_combos$race2[i]
  
    var_suffix <- paste(race1, race2, sep = "_")
    var_suffix <- str_replace(var_suffix, "/", ".")
    
    var_name <- paste0("inter_", var_suffix)                 
    mar_data <- mar_data |>
      mutate({{ var_name }} := (race_husband == race1 & race_wife == race2))
  
  if(race1 != "White") {
    # we need a gender adjuster
    var_name <- paste0("gender_", var_suffix)
    mar_data <- mar_data |>
      mutate(
        {{ var_name }} := case_when(
          race_husband == race1 & race_wife == race2 ~ 1,
          race_husband ==  race2 & race_wife ==  race1 ~ -1,
          TRUE ~ 0
        )
      )
  }
  
}
```


```{r}

model_recipe <- recipe(freq ~ ., data = mar_data) |>
  step_select(race_husband, race_wife, starts_with("inter_"), starts_with("gender_"), year) |>
  step_interact(terms = ~ (race_husband+race_wife+starts_with("inter_")+starts_with("gender_"))*year)

#model_recipe |> prep() |> formula()

model <- glm(freq~(race_husband + race_wife + (inter_White_Black + inter_White_AIAN + inter_White_API + inter_White_Hispanic
  + inter_Black_AIAN + inter_Black_API + inter_Black_Hispanic + inter_AIAN_API + inter_AIAN_Hispanic + inter_API_Hispanic +
  inter_White.Black_White + inter_White.Black_Black + inter_White.API_White + inter_White.API_API + inter_White.AIAN_White +
  inter_White.AIAN_AIAN) + (gender_Black_AIAN + gender_Black_API + gender_Black_Hispanic + gender_AIAN_API +
  gender_AIAN_Hispanic + gender_API_Hispanic + gender_White.Black_White + gender_White.Black_Black + gender_White.API_White +
  gender_White.API_API + gender_White.AIAN_White + gender_White.AIAN_AIAN)) * year, data = mar_data, family = poisson)

inter_lor <- avg_slopes(model, 
                        variables = c("inter_White_Black"), 
                        by = "year", 
                        type = "link")

inter_lor <- avg_slopes(model, 
                        variables = c("inter_White_Black", 
                                      "inter_White_AIAN",
                                      "inter_White_API",
                                      "inter_White_Hispanic",
                                      "inter_Black_API",
                                      "inter_Black_AIAN",
                                      "inter_Black_Hispanic",
                                      "inter_AIAN_API",
                                      "inter_API_Hispanic",
                                      "inter_AIAN_Hispanic"), 
                        by = "year", 
                        type = "link")

```
